lines: - Fixed an issue where a spec whose bundled file includes a large inline source map could crash the browser tab, leaving `cypress run` hanging with no error until it was killed. The crash could happen while the spec first loaded, or when it loaded again after its first [`cy.visit()`](https://on.cypress.io/visit) to another origin. Specs with inline source maps now also load faster and use less memory. Fixes [#35201](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/35201).

+- Fixed an issue where `cypress run` could hang until it was killed, or exit with an unrelated `socket hang up` error, when the process that loads your config file and runs your [Node events](https://docs.cypress.io/app/plugins/plugins-guide) exited, for example because the operating system ran out of memory or `setupNodeEvents` called `process.exit()`. In component testing this process also runs the dev server. Cypress now stops the run with an error that says the process exited, with its exit code or signal. Fixes [#25507](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/25507) and [#35223](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/35223).

- Fixed an issue where, in Chrome 158 and later, `cypress run` stopped with the error `* is not a valid URL` when it opened a second spec. Fixes [#35195](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/35195).

- Fixed an issue where, in Chrome 158 and later with [`injectDocumentDomain`](https://docs.cypress.io/app/references/configuration#e2e) enabled, navigating the application under test within [`cy.origin()`](https://on.cypress.io/origin) could fail with errors such as `Blocked a frame with origin` or `does not have permission to navigate the target frame`. Chrome 158 stopped firing `unload` events, which Cypress uses to track navigations. Fixed in [#35198](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/pull/35198).

- Fixed an issue where [`cy.intercept()`](https://on.cypress.io/intercept) silently ignored a header matcher when the same header name appeared more than once with different casing, such as `Content-Type` and `content-type`. Only the last matcher was applied. `cy.intercept()` now throws an error that names the duplicated header. Fixes [#34975](https://github.com/cypress-io/cypress/issues/34975).
